property.name: depart_text
property.value: You climb the old ladder back toward the lamp-smell of the Undercity.

property.name: text
property.value:
Square letters, cut deep, in the old tongue of the north. Someone has scratched a plainer version beneath.

KROVEN IS CROWNED WITH A SWORD.
WHAT THE KING CANNOT KEEP, THE GUARD KEEPS.

Beneath, in a shakier hand: We kept it. The king did not come down with us.

property.name: text
property.value: Armour gone green, a short sword still in the hand. The arrows around him are his own side's - fletched in Kroven grey.\n\nHe set the curtain himself, then walked into it so no one would have to come back and reset it.

property.name: text
property.value: Not Kroven. A Miravel buckle, a sack of nothing, a crowbar.\n\nWhoever came looking for the King's sword after the war learned what the alcoves in this hall are for. Too late.

property.name: text
property.value:
He took off his helm and set it beside him, very straight, and sat with his back to the water.

Scratched on the helm: NINE OF US CAME DOWN. THE SPIKES ARE FOR THEM, NOT FOR US. WE KNOW THE STEP.

The step: wait for the iron to sink, then walk behind it.

property.name: text
property.value:
Carved on the lid, worn smooth by no hand but the damp:

NOLAN, KING OF KROVEN. HE WAS CROWNED WITH A SWORD AND FELL HOLDING IT.

His guards brought him home in pieces, under the city that Borrow's men were burning. The sword they would not let the burners have.

property.name: key_got
property.value: Ironcrown. Below half health you take less damage and heavy blows cannot stagger you. The last cut of a combo leaves frost.

property.name: text
property.value: A sheathed blade of cold iron, the guard worked like a narrow crown. It lies across the stone before the King, where his guard set it down.\n\nKroven crowned its kings with a sword. This one was never given to another head.

property.name: hint_text
property.value: The Rampart Forms. Stand your ground: after a breath without moving, you take less damage until you step again.
